[P1] Do not allow completed units to reopen while remaining settled

After completing every unit, `unit start` accepts a previously completed unit. Its old `UNIT_COMPLETED` receipt remains in the settled set, so `next` returns the final `gate:true` directive even though that unit now has an active `UNIT_STARTED` checkpoint. Reject restarting a completed unit or make any nonterminal checkpoint override its earlier completion receipt and block approval.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
[P1] Make autonomy authorization check-and-consume atomic

`set-autonomy` calls `humanActedSinceGate()` before acquiring the audit lock, then appends `AUTONOMY_MODE_SET` and writes state in separate operations. Concurrent autonomy grants or an approval racing the grant can both observe the same fresh `HUMAN_TURN` and commit, violating the stated consume-once rule. Hold one lock across the presence check, audit append, and state update.

**P1 — Serialize contribution merges across plugin hooks**

_(Anchoring here on the new `scopes` sidecar record; the mutation this concerns is the `writeFileSync(stageFile)` at ~1480 and the sidecar write at ~1492.)_

I saw that each plugin's compose hook reads and rewrites the same stage file with no lock: the `writeFileSync(stageFile)` and the sidecar write both run unprotected, while the recompile at `aidlc-graph.ts:2160` already runs inside `withAuditLock`. So the transaction is only half-locked — two concurrent composes can both succeed and both write sidecars claiming their scope merged, but the last writer's stage file wins and silently drops the other plugin's `adds.scopes` merge.

I reproduced this with two simultaneous compose runs (the bun-fallback path a plugin's SessionStart hook takes when `aidlc` isn't on PATH): both exited 0, both sidecars were present, and the final stage contained only one scope. Please extend the existing `withAuditLock` to cover the whole stage + sidecar + compile transaction, not just the compile.

**P1 — Use the same lock for selection changes and compose**

I saw that `select-plugins` strips scopes and deletes the sidecar without coordinating with compose, so a concurrent compose can reintroduce a scope after its plugin is disabled.

My probe finished with `plugins: ["aidlc"]`, yet the disabled plugin's scope remained welded into the core stage and its sidecar was gone. Because re-enable + recompose never recreates the sidecar, no later disable can clean up that orphaned membership. Selection changes and compose need to share one lock.

**[BLOCKER] This runs write-mode package.ts against the real repo checkout.**

`writeHarness` rmSync's each committed `dist/<harness>` tree before rebuilding, and the integration tier runs files in parallel: sibling tests cpSync `dist/claude/.claude` and `dist/claude/aidlc` as their fixture base, and t145's `--check` byte-diffs the same trees, so this beforeAll opens a vanish-then-repopulate window under every parallel run. It also silently regenerates a stale committed dist mid-job (masking exactly the drift `--check` exists to catch) and leaves the checkout dirty. Every other packaging test builds into a temp dir under `--check` (t145).

Suggest a target-dir seam on package.ts (or reuse the `--check` temp-build path) so t188 never touches the committed trees; renaming the file `.serial.` alone would still leave the drift-masking.

Fixed in `7c00c7f`. Added a target-dir seam: `package.ts plugin build <plugin> <harness> <outDir>` renders one projection into an arbitrary dir via the pure `buildPluginProjection`. t188's beforeAll now builds the projection into its temp dir and composes from there — it never runs write-mode `package.ts` and never rmSyncs the committed trees. Verified the committed `dist/plugins/` is byte-identical before/after a t188 run.
